question: The Ullal de l’Estany is a Mediterranean wetland area of significant environmental value that is home to a wide variety of flora and fauna. It is also part of the Natura 2000 network. Along with other ullals, it supplies the Marjal de Gandía with water all year round. The Ullal de l’Estany is located in the Marjal de la Safor, a wetland area spanning 1 225.34 hectares that is part of the Natura 2000 network.

It is also classed as a site of Community importance (SCI Marjal de la Safor) and as a special protection area (SPA Montdúver-Marjal de la Safor). There are plans to build an Ohai glamping site in this location. The building project is being advertised as sustainable, but it will cover an area of 188 707m2 inside a protected zone and could well increase the number of tourists by 100 000 per year. 1.
Is the Commission aware that this building project is being planned for an area of protected wetland?
Is the Commission concerned about potential non-compliance with the directives on habitats and, if applicable, air quality?

How will the Commission ensure that protected areas – such as, in this case, the Natura 2000 network and a SPA – are indeed protected when the public authorities themselves are not abiding by the directives concerned?
answer: Under the Habitats Directive (1), any plan or project likely to have a significant effect on a Natura 2000 site shall be subject to appropriate assessment of its implications for the site in view of the site's conservation objectives. The competent national authorities shall agree to the plan or project only after having ascertained that it will not adversely affect the integrity of the site concerned.

In addition, Member States must take appropriate steps to avoid, in Natura 2000 sites, the deterioration of natural habitats and the habitats of species, as well as significant disturbance of the species for which the areas have been designated. Moreover, Member States must ensure that the species protection regime under the Habitats and Birds Directives (2) is respected.

The Commission was not aware of this project, and observes that, from the information provided by the Honourable Member, the project has not yet been authorised. It is therefore not possible to establish an infringement of the above provisions at this early stage in the procedure.

In any case, without prejudice of the Commission’s role as guardian of the Treaties, Member States are primarily responsible for the correct implementation of EU environmental legislation. In line with its policy approach (3), the Commission prioritises its enforcement efforts on cases which reveal a systematic breach of EU law in a Member State.
Using the means of redress provided under Spanish law would be the most appropriate and efficient way to challenge the legality of any future decision adopted in relation with this project.

Council Directive 92/43/EEC of 21 May 1992 on the conservation of natural habitats and of wild fauna and flora. OJ L 206, 22.7.1992, p. 7-50. Directive 2009/147/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 30 November 2009 on the conservation of wild birds. OJ L 20, 26.1.2010, p. 7-25.

As set out in Communication from the Commission ‘EU law Better results through better application’ (2017/C 18/02), 13 December 2016 and in Communication of 13 October 2022 COM(2022) 518 final — Enforcing EU law for a Europe that delivers.
